title: Sort Concentric Matrix Rings
description:
You are given an `m x n` integer matrix `grid`. The matrix can be decomposed into concentric rectangular layers (rings) starting from the outermost border (`layer = 0`) and moving inward.

Read each concentric layer in **clockwise** order starting from its top-left corner `(layer, layer)`: left-to-right along its top edge, top-to-bottom along its right edge, right-to-left along its bottom edge, and bottom-to-top along its left edge. (If the innermost layer degenerates to a single row, single column, or single cell, read those cells left-to-right or top-to-bottom without duplicates.)

Sort the values within each layer independently in **non-decreasing** order, write them back along the same clockwise order of that layer, and return the resulting matrix.
hints: Process layers from top = 0, left = 0 inward while top <= bottom and left <= right, collecting the coordinates of the current layer in clockwise order.
Sort the collected values for that layer and assign them back to the exact same sequence of coordinates.

examples.explanation: The outer ring of 8 elements [9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2] sorts clockwise into [2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9], while the single center cell 1 stays at (1, 1).
In a 2x4 matrix there is a single ring of 8 cells; sorting clockwise places the smallest values along the top row left-to-right and the largest along the bottom row right-to-left.
A single-row matrix has one degenerate ring of 4 cells sorted left-to-right.
